title: Machine learning identifies clinical sepsis phenotypes that translate to the plasma proteome.
summary: In 384 prospective multicenter sepsis patients, clinical-data clustering identified three severity phenotypes; plasma proteomics characterized them and supervised ML classified them. This is an observational phenotype result, not evidence of treatment benefit. The reviewed source supports this bounded result; external generalization, causal effects, and sustained operational impact remain unestablished where the source reports retrospective or internal evaluation.
ai_technology: unsupervised clustering/PCA of routine ICU clinical variables defines phenotypes; supervised Random Forest classifies phenotypes, and mass-spectrometry proteomics characterizes them.

evidence.tested: 384 prospective sepsis patients formed three severity phenotypes with different SOFA/mortality trajectories and corresponding plasma-proteome patterns.
evidence.unknown: Methods: 70/30 training/test split and 100-iteration Monte Carlo cross-validation for classifier evaluation. The observed multicenter clinical outcomes and proteomics support phenotype characterization; this does not show a treatment effect.
